label: <DEL> delimiter step of long sequences (L >= 6)
explanation: Fires on the <DEL> delimiter step, the step that outputs the first original token. 92% of activation mass is at the delimiter. The firing rate and magnitude grow with sequence length: rarely active for L <= 5, about 25% of steps active at t=8 and the most mass at t=8-9 (L=8,9), and the top activations (~0.43) are all at <DEL> of L=8-9 sequences. Within L=6 the rate also depends somewhat on the first token: lower when it is a/m/p/u/w/x/o/d/i/c/0/2, and adding that clause raises dev F1 to 0.82. Weaker secondary activity sits on the last 1-3 original tokens of long sequences (orig_idx 7-8, mostly first occurrences, about 7% of mass). Almost silent during the copy phase (0.4% of mass) and at t < 3. Dev: P 0.78, R 0.80, F1 0.79, mass recall 0.90.

issues: Main claim holds: the <DEL> step carries 91.9% of activation mass, the unit never fires at t<3, the copy phase carries 0.4% of mass, and the top activations are at the <DEL> of L=8-9 sequences.

The 'L >= 6' cutoff in the label and predicate is too generous. At L=6 the <DEL> step is active only 39% of the time (precision 0.39, about 10k false positives on dev). L=7 is 0.78, L=8 is 0.97, L=9 is 0.99. Most of the predicate's false positives come from L=6, so 'long sequences (L>=6)' overclaims for L=6.

The first-token effect is systematic and graded, and it is not limited to L=6 as the explanation says. Precision at <DEL> by first token at L=6 runs from 0.01 ('o') to 0.85 ('j','s'). At L=7 it runs from 0.21 ('o') and 0.40 ('d') to 0.99+ ('j','r','y'). So the unit behaves like a length-dependent drive plus an offset set by the first token, and a hard L threshold misses that.
The explanation's 'low' token list is only partly right. It includes p (L=6 precision 0.31) and x (0.33), which are middling. It leaves out q (0.09) and '3' (0.21), which are clearly low.
Test misses also include high-first-token L=5 <DEL> steps (for example j at 0.48, s at 0.57) and last-original-token steps at orig_idx 8 (precision 0.27, about 5% of mass). Both are secondary.
With first-token identity added, the improved predicate reaches test F1 0.825, above the 0.8 bar. The original verdict leaned on mass recall alone with F1 0.79.
skeptic.revised_label: <DEL> delimiter step: strength grows with sequence length and depends on the first token being recalled (reliably active for L>=8; at L=6-7 mainly when the first token is j/s/y/e/b/r/n/k/h/z/1)
